guide.summary: Public agent app, own OAuth app, over 25 users (app review, wait 2-4 weeks); Prototype or small pilot, up to 25 users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Prototype or small pilot, up to 25 users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Public agent app, own OAuth app, over 25 users (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for YNAB. Users see Composio's name on the consent screen unless you bring your own app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed YNAB app. For launch, use your own app if you want your brand on the consent screen or a dedicated quota. Your own app also needs YNAB review to pass 25 outside users.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of Composio's
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across Composio users
Managed apps are the default when available, so own app is optional

prerequisites.title: A YNAB account
prerequisites.detail: Any signed-in YNAB account can create an OAuth app in Developer Settings. No developer program, plan or region requirement is named.

prerequisites.title: Published privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: It must be shown to users, include a way to delete data on request (an email is fine), and its URL must be in the OAuth client configuration and in your app interface.

prerequisites.title: End users need an active YNAB subscription
prerequisites.detail: API calls return 403 errors when the account's subscription has lapsed or trial expired.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app in YNAB
steps.detail: Sign in, open Account Settings, then Developer Settings, and create the app with your redirect URI. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret shown after saving.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom OAuth2 auth config for the ynab toolkit with your client ID and secret, using the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard. Request the read-only scope unless writes are needed.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Draft and publish privacy policy
steps.detail: Agent drafts the policy with the required items; you publish it and add the URL to the OAuth app and your interface. YNAB does not check its legal compliance.
steps.done_when: Policy URL is live and set in the OAuth app.

steps.title: Check naming and terms compliance
steps.detail: Review the app name and domain against the 'for YNAB' naming rule and the API Terms.
steps.done_when: Name and domain follow the rules.

steps.title: Submit the review request form
steps.detail: Submit YNAB's review request form for your app.

steps.title: Wait for YNAB review
steps.detail: YNAB states 2-4 weeks. It emails you when Restricted Mode is removed.

traps.title: Hard stop at 25 outside users
traps.detail: Once the cap is reached, the authorization screen shows a message and new authorizations are blocked. Request review well before you approach it.

traps.title: Implicit grant tokens expire after 2 hours
traps.detail: The implicit grant has no refresh tokens, so users must re-authorize. The authorization code grant supports refresh tokens.

traps.title: Terms violations disable the app
traps.detail: Failing the API Terms or OAuth Application Requirements results in the app being disabled.

traps.title: Rate limit of 200 requests per hour
traps.detail: An access token can make up to 200 requests per hour, reset each clock hour. Plan agent call volume accordingly.

blockers.symptom: Authorization screen shows a message and new users cannot authorize
blockers.what_it_means: The Restricted Mode cap of 25 outside-user tokens has been reached.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit the review request form and wait for approval.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare the review submission details and check compliance.

blockers.symptom: 403 unauthorized_scope or 403 Forbidden on a write call
blockers.what_it_means: The token was issued with the read-only scope.
blockers.what_to_do: Re-authorize without read-only if writes are needed.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check which scope the auth config requests.

open_questions: Which review criteria beyond the Terms and Requirements does YNAB apply? Ask YNAB API support or read the OAuth Application Requirements.
Is there a customer-side admin requirement? None found; YNAB is per-user consent, so confirm with YNAB.
Does Composio's managed app count toward a shared token cap? Not found; ask Composio support.

evidence.quote: Your privacy policy must include, but is not limited to, the following:
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must include the listed items, such as how data is handled and stored, how long it is kept, and a last-updated date.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: A method for users to delete their data if they request it (can be a contact email).
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must give users a method to delete their data on request, which can be a contact email.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Display the privacy policy URL in your OAuth client configuration when your application is publicly available and ensure that it is prominently displayed in your application interface so that users can find this information easily.
evidence.answer: When publicly available, the privacy policy URL must be shown in the OAuth client configuration and prominently in the app interface.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: YNAB is not responsible for reviewing your Privacy Policy and determining whether it is compliant with all applicable privacy laws.
evidence.answer: YNAB states it does not review the developer's privacy policy for compliance with privacy laws.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: When an OAuth application is requesting authorization, a scope parameter with a value of read-only can be passed to request read-only access to a plan.
evidence.answer: The page documents only one scope: read-only, which requests read-only access to a plan.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If an access token issued with the read-only scope is used when requesting an endpoint that modifies the plan (POST, PATCH, etc.) a 403 Forbidden response will be issued.
evidence.answer: A read-only token that calls a write endpoint (POST, PATCH, etc.) receives a 403 Forbidden response.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If you do not need write access to a plan, please use the read-only scope.
evidence.answer: The page advises using the read-only scope when write access is not needed.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: The supplied access token has a scope which does not allow access.
evidence.answer: An API error (403 unauthorized_scope) is returned when a token's scope does not allow the requested access.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This means the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner.
evidence.answer: Unreviewed apps are capped at 25 access tokens for users other than the owner.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Once this limit is reached, a message will be placed on the Authorization screen and new authorizations will be prohibited.
evidence.answer: Once the 25-token cap is reached, the Authorization screen shows a message and new authorizations are prohibited.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type does not support refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the user must be prompted again to authorize your application.
evidence.answer: With the implicit grant, an access token expires 2 hours after being granted and there are no refresh tokens, so the user must re-authorize.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type supports refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the application can request a new access token without having to prompt the user to authorize again.
evidence.answer: With the authorization code grant, an access token expires 2 hours after being granted, but a refresh token allows a new one without re-prompting the user.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This new token will not expire but can be revoked at any time from this same screen.
evidence.answer: A Personal Access Token does not expire but can be revoked at any time.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour .
evidence.answer: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour; the page states this as a general limit, not one specific to unreviewed apps.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: The Restricted Mode removal review takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The subscription for this account has lapsed
evidence.answer: API calls return a 403 subscription_lapsed error when the YNAB account's subscription has lapsed.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The trial for this account has expired
evidence.answer: API calls return a 403 trial_expired error when the YNAB account's trial has expired.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The user will be given the option to approve your request for access:
evidence.answer: When an end user authorizes the app, they are given the option to approve the request for access.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When default plan selection is enabled, a user will be asked to select a default plan when authorizing your application:
evidence.answer: If default plan selection is enabled, the user is asked to choose a default plan when authorizing the app.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: An OAuth application can optionally have 'default plan selection' enabled.
evidence.answer: Default plan selection is an optional setting on an OAuth application.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: replacing [CLIENT_ID] and [REDIRECT_URI] with the values configured when creating the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The client ID and redirect URI are set when the OAuth application is created, and the authorization request must use those values.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri - The same [REDIRECT_URI] sent with the original authorization code request in Step 1 above and specified when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The redirect_uri in the token request must match the one sent in the authorization request and specified in the app setup.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: the user's browser will be redirected to the [REDIRECT_URI] with a new authorization code sent as a query parameter named code .
evidence.answer: After approval, the browser is redirected to the redirect URI with the authorization code as a query parameter named code.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After saving, you will see the details of the new application, including the Client ID and the Client Secret which are referenced in the instructions below.
evidence.answer: After saving the new application, its details show the Client ID and Client Secret.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_secret - The client secret provided when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The client secret is supplied in the token request as the value provided when the OAuth application was set up.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: These include scope , state , and code_challenge (PKCE).
evidence.answer: The authorization request can include the scope, state, and code_challenge (PKCE) security parameters.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: This means the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner.
evidence.answer: Restricted Mode caps the app at 25 access tokens for users other than the owner until it is removed.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: All OAuth Application integrations must abide by the API Terms of Service and the OAuth Application Requirements .
evidence.answer: All OAuth integrations must follow the API Terms of Service and OAuth Application Requirements, and failure to do so results in the app being disabled.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Failure to do so will result in disabling of the application.
evidence.answer: Failure to follow the terms and requirements results in disabling of the application.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application and the web address (DNS name) must not include "YNAB" or "You Need A Budget" unless preceded by the word "for".
evidence.answer: The application and its web address must not include 'YNAB' or 'You Need A Budget' unless preceded by the word 'for'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.
evidence.answer: Apps may not copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB using the API.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: To use the YNAB API and accept the Terms you must be of a legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB.
evidence.answer: Users must be of legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB to use the API.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application may not be directed or for children under 13.
evidence.answer: The application may not be directed at or for children under 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application must not directly request, handle or store any financial account credentials other than an access token obtained directly from a financial institution using OAuth.
evidence.answer: The application may not store financial account credentials other than an access token obtained through OAuth.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may only be used when permission is explicitly given by a YNAB account owner through the Authentication processes described in the documentation above.
evidence.answer: The API may be used only when a YNAB account owner has explicitly given permission through the documented authentication processes.
